A04 narrates ordering Super Saturated after a sister’s introduction and favorable experience, buying Buffer Jelly for richer nighttime hydration/repair, then buying the face wash and newly released mesh moisturizer. The last two resolve contextually to Plasma Wash and Molecular Mesh; precise purchased variants/formulas remain unknown. A05 explicitly checked out Avant Guard after TikTok discovery, within a stated sustainability motivation. A11 explicitly stocked up on Softwear during months of loving it. Favorable experience accompanying further Experiment acquisition repeats across two credited retailer-review origins, A04 and A11; their specific products and reasons differ. Creator-linked checkout has one focal narrator, A05. Neither establishes population-level causation or a generally repeated reason for purchasing any particular SKU.

A01 reports Softwear cart readdition because of a comment, not checkout. A12’s cream 2.0 and cleanser acquisitions concern Regimen Lab, resolved by the parent post. A14 received Buffer Jelly free for review and describes conversion after two uses, not purchase. A16 intends Continuum to replace two routine products; replacement and repurchase are not completed. A04’s claim that makeup remover is no longer needed establishes functional redundancy, not demonstrated discontinuation. A02 reports habitual omission of another brand’s exfoliator; A05 reports having stopped conventional sheet masks and subsequently incorporating the reusable mask. Those actual routine changes do not establish completed Experiment repurchase.

Consequences are materially mixed. A11’s Softwear stock-up and affection coexist with reported dermatitis, prescribed steroid treatment, and a worse flare within 24 hours of retrying; three unopened tubes and $70 CAD are reported stranded stock/value, not three inferred purchase events. The reviewer still recommends trying it with caution. This is individual causal attribution, not independently established medical causation. A15 considered returning Plasma Wash because of severe eye burning, while also reporting inadequate cleansing and dryness despite varied techniques; no completed return is narrated. This opposes A04’s favorable face-wash cleansing/hydration report. A14’s favorable Buffer Jelly result involved mixing it into moisturizer, limiting attribution to Buffer Jelly alone.

All six focal Junip reviews have 0 up-votes and 0 down-votes, with engagement observation time unavailable. These are distinct context accounts in one shared conversation, not additional focal sources. Engagement observation times and resonance materiality are unavailable.
